title: Unbounded winding around gamma obstructs the cut-and-glue approach
body:
## What goes wrong

A candidate surface with corners in the cut-open surface may have a boundary component
that comes in along one arc of C, winds around gamma a very large and uncontrolled number
of times, and then goes out along another arc of C.

Because that winding number is not bounded a priori, the search for gluable surfaces is
not obviously a search over a finite set of possibilities, and the linear programming
argument that settles the free case does not directly apply.
author: danny
what_was_tried:
Cut the surface along a simple essential curve gamma, decomposing the chain C into arcs in
the cut-open surface, and look for surfaces with corners there which glue along gamma into
an admissible surface for C. The cutting and the local combinatorics are fine; it is
controlling how far a boundary component can wind around gamma before leaving that is not.
